messages:
Jamie: Heads-up: getting repeated Xid(31) and growing ECC correctable counters on nodes gpu-r21-2 and gpu-r21-5 in rack r21. Pods flapping on a couple of inference fleets.

Priya: Can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and kernel logs? Also which vendor lot?

Jamie: Snippet from gpu-r21-2:
``nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0:
  ECC Errors
    Volatile
      ECC Count: 62
      Single Bit: 62
``
`dmesg | grep -i NVRM` shows multiple lines: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31` and a `Xid 79` near high-memory ops.

infra-bot: AUTO: incident created (INC-2025-210). Node gpu-r21-2 cordon recommended.

Nathan: Those GPUs are from PO RWD-598, vendor lot BATCH-99. We had a small bump in procurement then. I'm pulling serials.

Lin: I'm starting a soft-drain on gpu-r21-2 to avoid hard evictions: `kubectl cordon gpu-r21-2 && kubectl drain gpu-r21-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

Mel: Repro plan: we'll run stress test on a staging card from the same lot: `stress-ng --gpu 1 --timeout 45m` and monitor ECC; also run memory-heavy transformer decode load.

Priya: Initial hypothesis: marginal memory hardware in BATCH-99 causes spike in single-bit ECC; older firmware (470.80) on those cards might be exposing it. If errors accumulate they lead to Xid and driver reset affecting pods.

Jamie: Impact summary: 2 nodes soft-drained, ~12 pod restarts, estimated 5% gen-4 GPU capacity loss in eu-central-1 for ~4 hours. No customer-facing SLA breach but internal perf degradation for some jobs.

procurement-bot: RMA ticket RMA-8031 opened with vendor. Expedited replacement requested.

Nathan: Action items: 1) inventory sweep for BATCH-99 and mark as watchlist (owner: Nathan). 2) Enforce scheduling hold for BATCH-99 until validated (owner: Lin). 3) Fleet firmware uplift to 470.103 for at-risk pool (owner: Priya). 4) Auto-soft-drain on ECC_correctable > 25/hr (owner: eng-infra tooling).

Lin: I've added racks r20-r22 to temporary alerting and increased ECC sampling resolution to 5m.

Mel: Stress reproducer in staging (same lot) caused ECC correctable to climb to 48 after ~22m and triggered driver reset with Xid 31 after 27m. Repro is consistent on two different cards from BATCH-99.

Priya: Strong signal. We'll proceed with blocking scheduling on those serials and coordinate RMA replacements. Also pushing firmware test matrix to see if uplift reduces incidences.

Jamie: Drafting RCA: cause = recurring DRAM margin/recurring silicon defect in vendor lot BATCH-99 exacerbated by older firmware handling under sustained memory pressure -> single-bit ECC accumulation -> Xid resets -> pod evictions.

Nathan: Mitigations applied: soft-drain thresholds, temporary scheduling hold on BATCH-99, RMA request, monitoring dashboards updated, procurement to tag incoming serials.

Priya: Follow-ups: full fleet scan for same firmware + lot (TASK-2025-3321), automated alert+soft-drain rollout (TASK-2025-3322), vendor RCA request and credit negotiation (TASK-2025-3323).

procurement-bot: Procurement will require vendor lot metadata and perform stricter QA on arrival.

Jamie: Will put the final RCA into #incidents and update the SRE runbook with the new soft-drain play. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Lin: Note for playbook: always check `lspci -v` + vendor lot before scheduling new GPU nodes; add gate on intake.

Mel: I'll run extended firmware A/B tests tomorrow and report results.

Priya: Closing thread; will link the formal RCA doc and tasks. :white_check_mark:
